symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two address chunks.
symbols.quote: it swaps two disjoint address fields, chunks, of $u$ bits each (here $u$ is the chunk width in bits, not the input sequence as on the [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) page) in an array of $V$ stored bits (a volume, not a label)

symbols.name: address prefix
symbols.meaning: The prefix field of an address, before the first chunk.
symbols.quote: An address is $(p,h,g,d,z)$ with prefix $p$ (here $p$ means the address prefix, not the number of fractional bits as on the [Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md) page), chunks $h$ and $d$ (here $h$ means the first address chunk, not the remaining index as on the [Butterflies and the fast transform](butterfly.md) page nor the ground-set size as on the exchange-network page, and $d$ means the second address chunk, not the number of axes as on the [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) page), gap $g$, suffix $z$; the goal is $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$. Digits are radix $q$, a fixed prime (here $q$ means the digit radix, not a sequence length as on the discrete Fourier transform and cyclic convolution pages).

symbols.name: first chunk
symbols.meaning: The first of the two address chunks being interchanged.
symbols.quote: An address is $(p,h,g,d,z)$ with prefix $p$ (here $p$ means the address prefix, not the number of fractional bits as on the [Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md) page), chunks $h$ and $d$ (here $h$ means the first address chunk, not the remaining index as on the [Butterflies and the fast transform](butterfly.md) page nor the ground-set size as on the exchange-network page, and $d$ means the second address chunk, not the number of axes as on the [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) page), gap $g$, suffix $z$; the goal is $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$. Digits are radix $q$, a fixed prime (here $q$ means the digit radix, not a sequence length as on the discrete Fourier transform and cyclic convolution pages).

symbols.name: second chunk
symbols.meaning: The second of the two address chunks being interchanged.
symbols.quote: An address is $(p,h,g,d,z)$ with prefix $p$ (here $p$ means the address prefix, not the number of fractional bits as on the [Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md) page), chunks $h$ and $d$ (here $h$ means the first address chunk, not the remaining index as on the [Butterflies and the fast transform](butterfly.md) page nor the ground-set size as on the exchange-network page, and $d$ means the second address chunk, not the number of axes as on the [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) page), gap $g$, suffix $z$; the goal is $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$. Digits are radix $q$, a fixed prime (here $q$ means the digit radix, not a sequence length as on the discrete Fourier transform and cyclic convolution pages).

symbols.name: gap
symbols.meaning: The address field between the two chunks.
symbols.quote: An address is $(p,h,g,d,z)$ with prefix $p$ (here $p$ means the address prefix, not the number of fractional bits as on the [Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md) page), chunks $h$ and $d$ (here $h$ means the first address chunk, not the remaining index as on the [Butterflies and the fast transform](butterfly.md) page nor the ground-set size as on the exchange-network page, and $d$ means the second address chunk, not the number of axes as on the [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) page), gap $g$, suffix $z$; the goal is $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$. Digits are radix $q$, a fixed prime (here $q$ means the digit radix, not a sequence length as on the discrete Fourier transform and cyclic convolution pages).

symbols.name: suffix
symbols.meaning: The address field after the second chunk.
symbols.quote: An address is $(p,h,g,d,z)$ with prefix $p$ (here $p$ means the address prefix, not the number of fractional bits as on the [Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md) page), chunks $h$ and $d$ (here $h$ means the first address chunk, not the remaining index as on the [Butterflies and the fast transform](butterfly.md) page nor the ground-set size as on the exchange-network page, and $d$ means the second address chunk, not the number of axes as on the [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) page), gap $g$, suffix $z$; the goal is $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$. Digits are radix $q$, a fixed prime (here $q$ means the digit radix, not a sequence length as on the discrete Fourier transform and cyclic convolution pages).

symbols.name: digit radix
symbols.meaning: The fixed prime radix of the stored digits.
symbols.quote: Digits are radix $q$, a fixed prime (here $q$ means the digit radix, not a sequence length as on the discrete Fourier transform and cyclic convolution pages).

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent below 1 in the interchange cost, equal to 1 - 2^{-50}.
symbols.quote: where $\tau=1-2^{-50}$ is the saving exponent

symbols.name: digit count
symbols.meaning: The number of radix-q digits in each chunk.
symbols.quote: Let each chunk have $e=m^k$ digits, with $k$ recursion levels (not the depth of a value).

symbols.name: recursion levels
symbols.meaning: The number of recursion levels, with e = m^k.
symbols.quote: Let each chunk have $e=m^k$ digits, with $k$ recursion levels (not the depth of a value).

symbols.name: vertex matrix
symbols.meaning: The rational m by m matrix carried by a terminal or gate of the network.
symbols.quote: each terminal and gate carries a rational $m\times m$ matrix $M$ (here $M$ means the vertex matrix of the network, not the number of cyclic addresses as on the cyclic convolution page), and edge $i$ carries $A_i=M_{\mathrm{head}(i)}-M_{\mathrm{tail}(i)}$

symbols.name: edge matrix
symbols.meaning: The difference of the matrices at the two ends of edge i.
symbols.quote: each terminal and gate carries a rational $m\times m$ matrix $M$ (here $M$ means the vertex matrix of the network, not the number of cyclic addresses as on the cyclic convolution page), and edge $i$ carries $A_i=M_{\mathrm{head}(i)}-M_{\mathrm{tail}(i)}$

symbols.name: output role
symbols.meaning: The output role to which input wire w is routed.
symbols.quote: The shear contract: input wire $w$ is routed to an output role $\rho(w)$ with $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$

symbols.name: wire index
symbols.meaning: The index of an input wire of the network.
symbols.quote: The shear contract: input wire $w$ is routed to an output role $\rho(w)$ with $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$

symbols.name: address shear
symbols.meaning: The array permutation moving the entry at address (H,D) to (H+MD,D).
symbols.quote: Let $\Phi_M$ move the entry at address $(H,D)$ to $(H+MD,D)$

symbols.name: wire input
symbols.meaning: The physical input array of wire w.
symbols.quote: Read wire $w$'s input $f_w$ as the logical array $\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w$.

symbols.name: stream row number
symbols.meaning: The row number within a role stream.
symbols.quote: row $Wx+w-1$ goes to stream $w$ as row $x$ (here $x$ means the stream row number, not a vector of $F$ as on the nested-subspace-labels page)

symbols.name: recursion level index
symbols.meaning: An index of a recursion level in the unrolled sum.
symbols.quote: Unrolled over the recursion levels $j$ (here $j$ means a recursion level index, not a digit value as on the elementary-stream-operations page, a wrap count as on the controlled-shifts page, or a stage number as on the nested-subspace-labels page)

symbols.name: levels needed
symbols.meaning: The number of recursion levels needed for chunks of e digits.
symbols.quote: put $k'=\lceil\log_m e\rceil$, the number of levels needed

symbols.name: set-aside digits
symbols.meaning: The number of top digits of each chunk set aside to form the row field.
symbols.quote: let $\nu=\lceil k'\log W/(2\log q)\rceil$ be the number of top digits of each chunk set aside

symbols.name: row range
symbols.meaning: The range of the row field formed by the top digits of both chunks.
symbols.quote: Now $d^+,h^+$ form a row field of range $\Lambda=q^{2\nu}\ge W^{k'}$ before both remaining chunks.

symbols.name: padded row count
symbols.meaning: The row count after padding with zero rows to a multiple of W^{k'}.
symbols.quote: Pad with zero rows to $\Lambda'=W^{k'}\lceil \Lambda/W^{k'}\rceil<2\Lambda$ rows, so the volume stays below $2V$.

symbols.name: piece count
symbols.meaning: The number of pieces of width m^j into which each remaining chunk is cut.
symbols.quote: where the base-$m$ digit $a_j$ is the number of pieces of width $m^j$ into which each remaining chunk is cut

relations.quote: So the time per unit volume $F_k$ at width $m^k$ obeys $F_0=O(1)$, $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, the recurrence of [Recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md).
The interchange performs each edge shear by [Matrix shear by triangular factorization](matrix-shear.md): if $A_i$ has rank $a$, then $\Phi_{A_i}$ costs $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit fields
Rows are split into role streams by [Elementary stream operations](stream-ops.md)

derivations.quote: So the time per unit volume $F_k$ at width $m^k$ obeys $F_0=O(1)$, $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, the recurrence of [Recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md).
The total is $O(V)\sum_ja_jm^{j\tau}\le O(V)\,m\sum_jm^{j\tau}=O(Ve^\tau)$, since $m^{k'}<me$ makes $\sum_jm^{j\tau}$ a geometric sum.
